_readme: INTEGRATION FIXTURE. A test asset, not a seed: `data/` stays the
only seed directory and `scripts/seed.ts` its only reader. The
integration seed reads this directory and nothing under `data/`,
on top of a `db:seed` pass that has already written the domain.
This file carries `export_subscriptions` rows for the example
domain, each transcribed from the web fixture module named in its
`_comment`, so the web's fixture path and a seeded `ar_live` tell
one story. Keys beginning with an underscore are commentary, not
columns.
`fixtureId` is not a column. The database issues
`export_subscriptions.id`; the member keeps the `id` the web
fixture gave the row. (`domainSlug`, `format`, the connector) is
the natural key
`export_subscriptions_domain_id_format_connector_id_unique` holds. `connectorKind` and `connectorName` name a row of
`connectors.json` by (`kind`, `name`), the natural key
`connectors_kind_name_unique` holds, rather than by a database id.
TIMESTAMPS ARE FIXED. `nextRunAt` is copied from the web fixture as
written, against the web's `FIXTURE_NOW` of
`2026-06-11T14:30:00.000Z`, and never derived from the wall clock.
Seeded into a database whose clock has moved past them, every
non-null `nextRunAt` here reads as overdue; the rows keep the
stamps anyway, because a relative stamp would make two seeds of
one bundle differ. `nextRunAt` null means never scheduled, and is
not the overdue state subscription 3 is in.
